rv.q: I can’t say that I fully understand the themes the playwright attempts to unravel, but if you embrace the ambiguity, it’s an intriguing show.
If beauty is in the eye of the beholder, then it behooves you to behold this charming production.

Glassheart Through 2/23: Fri–Sat 7:30 PM, Sun 3 PM; also Mon 2/10 and 2/17 7:30 PM; City Lit Theater, 1020 W. Bryn Mawr, 773-293-3682, citylit.org , $35 ($30 seniors, $12 students and military) This desire becomes more than a pipe dream when Only meets their new neighbor, Aiofe (Cailyn Murray), who has come to start a new life in Chicago.
With quirky characters, fun banter, and tons to look at, you are going to love seeing things from a new angle.
This is essentially a one-set drawing room production, well written and well directed with solid performances by everyone.
If you’re intrigued by a retelling that explores deeper questions and set in a modern day world, Glassheart would be a good fit for you.
But Evans’ dynamism and sheer force of will are not enough to save this confusing work of magical realism that projects a French fairytale from the 18th century onto our world today.
